title: POC scoping - success criteria signoff

Schedule live benchmark run and go/no-go review with execs (tentative 2025-10-10)
Share security pack and SOC2 evidence link
action_items: Priya Patel | Run k8s + Dedicated bench with 3 model variants, capture p95 latency and token cost | Due: 2025-10-07

summary: Redwood and Orion aligned on POC acceptance criteria: p95 latency < 800ms for 128-token responses (target), availability > 99.5%, model quality measured by human eval (>= 85% pass rate) and automated NLU metrics. Benchmarks to run on dedicated pool and hosted fallback; reporting via shared spreadsheet + Redwood dashboard. Two-week pilot with defined dataset; signoff requires meeting all go thresholds or documented mitigations.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-30
Time: 08:45 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Michael Torres (Orion CTO), Sara Liu (VP Eng), Nikhil Rao (ML Eng)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we wanted to use this slot to lock down the POC success criteria and acceptance tests so we can run the benchmark next week. Michael, Sara, did you get the preread?
[00:12] Michael Torres: Yeah thanks Alex, we skimmed it, looked reasonable. Main thing for us is latency under load and, uh, quality not regressing vs our current heuristic pipeline.
[00:22] Priya Patel: Cool, so quick agenda — agree go/no-go thresholds, confirm workload sizing (TPS, token mix), define benchmark runs and reporting format, define timeline and next steps. Sound good?
[00:31] Sara Liu: Sounds good. Also want to make sure the security checklist items are on the path — SSO/SAML and KMS, etc.
[00:36] Alex Chen: Yep we'll include the security pack; Priya will share the SOC2 evidence link.
[00:40] Nikhil Rao: One thing up front, our median request size is 112 tokens, 90th is ~420, but the majority are short clarifications — so we care about p95 and p99 for web latency.
[00:51] Priya Patel: Great detail, Nikhil. For the acceptance tests we usually define p50/p95 latencies, throughput under a target concurrency, error rate, and a quality bar measured in both automated metrics and human eval.
[01:02] Michael Torres: For go/no-go I'd say p95 < 800ms is our target, p95 < 1.2s is acceptable with documented mitigation, error rate < 1%, and quality human pass rate >= 85% on our validation set.
[01:18] Alex Chen: That's a clear start. Redwood's typical target for similar workloads on Dedicated is p95 around 400-700ms depending on model and batch config. We'll record both dedicated and hosted fallbacks.
[01:29] Sara Liu: Also curious about cost — we need token cost estimates for 1M requests/month baseline.
[01:33] Priya Patel: We'll include token-level cost breakdown in the report; the acceptance report will show cost per 1k tokens per model variant.
[01:40] Michael Torres: Ok, let's formalize the go/no-go thresholds now.
[01:44] Priya Patel: Drafting on the call: 1) Latency: p95 <= 800ms (target) ; p95 <= 1200ms (acceptable w/mitigations). 2) Availability: >= 99.5% during benchmark window. 3) Error rate (>= 4xx/5xx) < 1%. 4) Quality: Human eval pass >= 85% on 200 samples; Auto-metrics — intent-classification F1 >= 0.88 where applicable. 5) Cost: token cost not to exceed agreed threshold (TBD by cost spreadsheet).
[02:16] Nikhil Rao: 200 human eval samples — do you have a suggested rubric? We use a 3-point rubric right now: correct / partial / wrong.
[02:23] Priya Patel: That's fine; we'll map to pass if 'correct' or 'partial but acceptable' — we should align labels. Redwood will run blind evaluation with your labels.
[02:34] Michael Torres: Reporting format? We prefer a shared spreadsheet with per-run rows plus a dashboard snapshot.
[02:39] Alex Chen: Agreed. Redwood will deliver a spreadsheet with run metadata (model, quantization, batch size, concurrency, seed), raw latency histograms, token counts, and cost numbers. We'll also share a live Redwood dashboard view for the exec review.
[02:55] Sara Liu: For workload sizing, here's our expected profile — baseline: 1M requests/month, average tokens per request 120, peak concurrency 200, steady concurrency ~40. For the POC we'll scale down to a 48-hour concentrated run that simulates a 7-day peak: ramp to 200 concurrency for 30 minutes, sustained 100 for 2 hours, etc.
[03:20] Priya Patel: That's very helpful. So benchmark plan: 1) baseline correctness run (single-user snapshots) 2) concurrency load run with ramp profile 3) resilience test — kill a pod and see failover 4) fallback routing test to hosted variant. We'll capture p50/p95/p99, throughput, and error rates per run.
[03:42] Michael Torres: Good. On the resilience test we need to quantify failover time — acceptable is under 30s to recover to previous throughput.
[03:50] Alex Chen: We'll include recovery time and tail latency impact.
[03:53] Nikhil Rao: What models will we try? We currently use an internally-tuned LLM, but open to trying open models and Redwood-verified ones.
[03:59] Priya Patel: For scoping, Redwood suggests testing three variants: 1) small/fast quantized variant (for low latency), 2) medium accuracy variant (balanced), 3) high-accuracy (bigger model). We'll record cost/latency/quality tradeoffs.
[04:12] Sara Liu: Ok please include quantization details and kernel choices in the report — our infra team cares about that for on-prem planning.
[04:20] Priya Patel: Noted. We'll include quantization level (8-bit/4-bit), inferred kernel choices, and any known incompatibilities. Note transcription: sometimes the model names get munged — we'll include precise model IDs in the spreadsheet.
[04:32] Michael Torres: On data privacy — we need KMS integration for keys and ensure logs are stored in our VPC.
[04:38] Alex Chen: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and VPC storage for logs; we'll provide the deployment checklist.
[04:44] Nikhil Rao: For acceptance tests, do you run the human eval internally or do we run it? We prefer to do it ourselves to own final pass/fail.
[04:51] Priya Patel: We can do either. Typical flow: Redwood produces the anonymized predictions and you run the human labels; Redwood can run a blind double-check. For signoff we recommend customer-owned labels as primary.
[05:05] Michael Torres: Fine. We'll own the final human eval. Redwood's pass/fail still needs to be reproducible and auditable.
[05:12] Alex Chen: We'll provide the raw outputs, diff tools, and the evaluation script.
[05:17] Sara Liu: Timeline? Can we do a 2-week POC starting 2025-10-06?
[05:22] Alex Chen: That works for Redwood on our side if we get logs by 2025-10-03. So timeline: 10/03 logs & samples; 10/06 bench runs start (48-72 hour concentrated runs); 10/10 exec review and signoff meeting.
[05:34] Priya Patel: I'll send a proposed run calendar and the spreadsheet template today.
[05:40] Nikhil Rao: On instrumentation, we need p95 across regions — most traffic is US-west but we want EU-aware numbers too. Can you run region-aware runs?
[05:48] Priya Patel: Yes, we can do separate runs for us-west and eu-west nodes; we'll mark them in the spreadsheet.
[05:54] Michael Torres: What about fallback policy? If Dedicated can't keep up, we want automatic fallback to hosted model variant with minimal disruption. How do you signal that in the acceptance criteria?
[06:06] Alex Chen: We'll test fallback as part of the resilience testing and measure user-perceived latency and error. Acceptance can allow fallback as long as overall user pass rate stays above threshold and documented mitigations exist.
[06:20] Sara Liu: Costs again — we'll need an estimated monthly run-rate extrapolated from benchmark numbers.
[06:25] Priya Patel: We'll include extrapolated token cost per month for each variant and include best practices to reduce token usage (prompt trimming, caching).
[06:33] Michael Torres: Ok let's make the acceptance test explicit in a single line that execs can sign: 'POC is successful if all of the following are met during the benchmark window: latency p95 <= 800ms OR documented mitigation; human eval >= 85%; error rate < 1%; availability >= 99.5%.'
[06:53] Priya Patel: I'll add a pass/fail column per criterion in the spreadsheet and an overall Go/No-Go recommendation row with notes.
[07:01] Alex Chen: Are there any blockers that would prevent us starting on 10/06?
[07:05] Michael Torres: We need to sanitize logs and remove PII — that's in progress, due 10/03. Also security review for KMS is on-going but shouldn't block the benchmark.
[07:17] Nikhil Rao: One detail — for human eval we want to weight certain intents more heavily (billing/helpdesk). Can we do stratified sampling?
[07:25] Priya Patel: Yes we can stratify the 200 samples by intent buckets you provide. Please include distribution with the logs.
[07:32] Sara Liu: Ok, on reporting format, please include a short executive summary slide set in addition to the sheet — 2 slides: Executive verdict and Key numbers.
[07:43] Alex Chen: We'll produce a 2-slide exec summary with the go/no-go and top three risks & mitigations.
[07:48] Michael Torres: Any concerns about test reproducibility? We need seed control and environment snapshots.
[07:53] Priya Patel: We'll include seed, model hash, container image, and infra snapshot in the run metadata.
[07:59] Nikhil Rao: For the resilience test, are you going to simulate pod failures or network partitions?
[08:04] Priya Patel: We'll simulate pod kill and a networking throttle for one run; both will be captured.
[08:10] Michael Torres: Great. If we pass with the medium model variant we may ask to move to Dedicated Reserved capacity — how long does that typically take?
[08:18] Alex Chen: Dedicated provisioning lead time depends on region; for US-west usually 2-3 weeks, can be sped up. We'll give commit options in the commercial proposal.
[08:26] Sara Liu: Anything else?
[08:28] Priya Patel: Quick recap of deliverables: Redwood sends spreadsheet template + security pack (today), customer sends logs by 10/03, Redwood runs benchmarks 10/06-10/08, deliver report + exec slides 10/09, signoff meeting 10/10. Action items listed in the doc.
[08:46] Michael Torres: That's good. We'll aim to have the logs and stratification notes to you by Friday.
[08:49] Alex Chen: Perfect, thanks all. We'll follow up in email and post the calendar invite for the signoff review.
[08:55] Sara Liu: Thanks everyone.
[09:00] Meeting ends.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mishearing of model names and kernel terms, some timestamps approximate.

References mentioned:
- Redwood POC spreadsheet template (link shared in chat)
- Redwood security pack & SOC2 evidence (link to be shared)
- Customer 48hr sanitized logs (to be uploaded to shared bucket)

Acceptance criteria (finalized on call):
- Latency: p95 <= 800ms target / <= 1200ms acceptable with mitigation
- Availability >= 99.5%
- Error rate < 1%
- Human eval pass rate >= 85% on 200 stratified samples (customer-labeled)
- Recovery time for simulated failure < 30s
- Reporting: shared spreadsheet + Redwood dashboard + 2-slide exec summary

Deliverables and timeline:
- 2025-10-02: Redwood sends acceptance report template and calendar invites
- 2025-10-03: Customer provides sanitized 48-hour logs, sample labels distribution
- 2025-10-06 to 10-08: Redwood runs benchmark suite (48-72h concentrated window)
- 2025-10-09: Redwood shares detailed report and exec slides
- 2025-10-10: Signoff meeting (go/no-go)
